judgment processes, making the reasoning trace useless as a diagnostic."],"shared_structure":["A system's reliability can be diagnosed by its behavior on boundary cases or conflict cases, not just on its overall success rate.","Process tracing (inspecting the reasoning) can distinguish between structural understanding and heuristic application."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["If the evaluation includes process data (reasons, justifications), one can distinguish compliance from competence by analyzing the content of those reasons on diagnostic cases.","The 'single evaluation' can be designed to include these diagnostic conflict cases and process-tracing requirements, making the distinction observable."]},"claim":"A within-evaluation distinction between genuine reliability and mere compliance is possible by analyzing the panel's reasoning traces on cases where the checklist and intuition conflict, checking whether the panel's agreement with the checklist is mediated by understanding or by rote adherence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel members are trained to produce convincing-sounding justifications regardless of their actual understanding.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'conflict cases' are not truly diagnostic of understanding and can be solved by applying the checklist without comprehension.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"While outcome alone cannot distinguish competence from luck, the process data can. If the evaluation includes cases where the checklist's recommendation conflicts with a plausible but incorrect intuition, and the panel follows the checklist, one can inspect the panel's justifications. If the justifications merely restate the checklist rule ('We chose X because item 3 says so'), this suggests compliance. If the justifications explain why the checklist rule is correct in this case ('We chose X because feature A, which the checklist item 3 targets, is the true cause of outcome Y'), this suggests understanding. Furthermore, one can look at cases where the checklist is ambiguous or silent and see whether the panel's judgments are coherent or random. Genuine reliability should produce coherent judgments even off-checklist; mere compliance should produce noise off-checklist.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
